speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim
text: asked the Minister for Trade and Industry whether there are plans to complement commercial supply of antigen rapid test (ART) kits from overseas suppliers with the increase in manufacturing capacity of locally produced ART kits.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: It is heartening to know that there are six companies that are keen to make or assembly ART kits here.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: I understand from a recent Straits Times article or report last year that there are, currently, two local manufactured ART kits that are being approved for use within a clinical setting with professional guidance, but they were not able to obtain the necessary validations for approval to sell on the retail market because most local hospitals are too busy to carry out clinical trials of the kits.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: First, will there be any particular consideration that could hold back the approval of these six companies' applications that have been announced?

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Second, what are the considerations when approving an ART kit for retail sale?

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Third, what steps are being taken to mitigate the risk posed by connectivity disruptions to ensure a good, steady and healthy supply of ART kits to Singapore?

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: Here, we have seen an increase in the demand for ART kits amidst the latest Omicron wave and also during the recent festive period.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: In addition, more Singaporeans are practising social responsibility with regular self-testing.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: So, to Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim's third question on ensuring the connectivity and continuous supply of ART kits, I want to reassure him and everyone in the House that the Government has been able to respond to heightened demand due to our multi-pronged strategy of diversification, stockpiling and also by working very closely with the importers, distributors, retailers to ensure that Singapore and Singaporeans have continual and sufficient supply of ART kits.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: During the recent spike of Omicron cases, MOH drew down on its stockpile to supplement the retailers' supply of testing kits.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: Prior to that, Members would probably remember that the Government distributed close to 25 million ART kits to households in Singapore just last year.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: If Members remember, the two distribution drives – the first was between August and September, and the second drive was between October and December – saw that each household received a total of 16 ART kits.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: So, I want to assure Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim that the Government spares no effort in ensuring the continued supply of ART kits which is critical to living in the new normal.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: So, we welcome the application of the six companies seeking to assemble or manufacture ART kits in Singapore.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: To his first two supplementary questions about testing, requirements and approval process required for retail sale, I want to share with Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim and Members that only ART kits that have been evaluated to meet the stringent standards of quality, safety and performance and, at the same time, verified for its accuracy when used by consumers, will be made available for retail sale.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: For example, ART kits have to undergo a separate route for approval where they are being benchmarked against PCR tests.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: Because MOH has explained that these self-test ART kits are to be used widely by members of the public in self-test settings.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: So, the implications on public health will be huge and significant if the kits that are approved for self-test are not sufficiently accurate.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: Besides the 12 self-test ART kits that have been approved by MOH and HSA for retail sales, I want to assure Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim that MOH is also actively evaluating other ART kits for their eligibility.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: Two other brands called Biocredit and Hotgen have obtained satisfactory analytical validation results and are in the midst of obtaining their PSAR registration prior to clinical validation.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: We hope that we will continue to have more options and wider supplies of ART kits from here as well as from abroad.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: Thirdly, we work very closely with various partners, importers, distributors and retailers to plan ahead and ensure that affordable stocks of ART kits are constantly on-stream for Singaporeans.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: I want to assure Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim that MTI, together with MOH and HSA, will continue to make the supply of ART kits our key priority and will provide ample support for the development and expeditious evaluation of ART kits, including local ones, to ensure quality self-test kits for Singapore's protection and safety.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Can I ask the Minister of State will the local manufacture of ART kits be expected to reduce the price of ART kits, which can benefit consumers?

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: I am asking this because the current price of over $5 per kit can still be a cost burden on many families who are all on quarantine or Health Risk Notice (HRN) and are expected to test regularly.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: I note from personal experience that a number of free ART kits given out at the vending machines to individuals on HRN seem to have been reduced from six to three.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
text: Can I confirm that this is the case?

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: I mentioned the multi-pronged approach and the third prong that I mentioned is that MTI will continue to work closely with our importers, distributors and retailers to bring in various brands of self-test ART kits and to give choice and options to consumers.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: Most recently, I went to either Guardian or Watsons, and you can buy an ART kit for about $4.90.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: At the same time, members of the public can make appointments at any of the QTCs and CTCs.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: So, I want to assure Mr Gerald Giam and Members in the House that we will press on with our multi-prong approach to ensure that Singaporeans have access to continued supply of ART self-test kits.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: Just one supplementary question, further to what my colleague Mr Gerald Giam was talking about.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: I heard one report that a PCR test was actually substantially cheaper in a neighbouring country, compared to Singapore.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: I am not sure how accurate that is or whether it is still the case.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: But my supplementary question is, looking at the countries in the region which have large populations, has the Government explored doing bulk purchase agreements, working together with other ASEAN countries, to negotiate with the manufacturers of these test kits, whether PCR or ART, as a way of lowering the price?

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: I want to assure him that an important part of our multi-prong approach is to diversify our import sources.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: So, we will press on with our efforts, not just in terms of importing from multiple sources to bring choice and, in general, to further lower the price of ART kits, but, at the same time, to work with local companies or Singapore-based companies which have the intention or interest to manufacture or assemble ART self-test kits here.
